messages.author: 0b01d1f6f2d73ae4
messages.subject: Simulated items producing no variability
parts:
Hi  Phil & Others,

I am working through simulating a nominal model, and then analyzing it with the graded.

Please find my some sample code below. I will likely be keeping sd's of 1 but the correlations/covariances will be shifting.

Theta<-rmvnorm(1000,sigma=matrix(c(1,.50,
                                   .50,1),2))
a<-matrix(c(rep(1.5,30),rep(.7,30),rep(.7,30),rep(1.5,30)),60)
d<-matrix(c(rep(0,60), rep(2,60),rep(1,60),rep(-1,60),rep(-2,60)),60)
d<-t(apply(d,1,sort, decreasing=TRUE))
poly<-simdata(a,d,1000,Theta=Theta,itemtype='nominal', mins=1)
model<-mirt.model('
                  F1=1-60
                  F2=1-60
                  MEAN=F1,F2
                  COV=F1*F2')
mod<-mirt(poly,model, itemtype='graded', technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))

I am finding that often when the data is simulated certain items will produce no variability and stop the model estimation.
Error: "Error: The following items have only one response category and cannot be estimated..."

This is less of a problem when one running one at a time, I can just keep simulating data until one is acceptable. But my next move is to automate simulated replications & analysis, and this will likely cramp the replications. Is there something I'm missing to ensure there is variability among the items?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Simulated items producing no variability
parts:
What are the scoring coefficients here? It seems the ak input was not provided (for a gpcm, the coef are by default 0, 1, 2, 3, .... , K-1....but for ordinal items these can vary to indicate which category is higher than which). The function should have thrown an error when the ak matrix isn't supplied when nominal items are included, so future versions will throw an error instead. HTH.

Phil
